summary: Connecticut's sitting governor, Ned Lamont (Democrat), ran again and won a third term, defeating state Sen. Ryan Fazio (Republican).

candidates.name: Ned Lamont
candidates.bio: Ned Lamont is a Democrat and the governor of Connecticut, seeking a third term in 2026. He is a Harvard graduate with a Yale MBA who started a Connecticut business serving college campuses, and he ran for U.S. Senate in 2006 against Joe Lieberman. He lives in Greenwich.

positions.summary: Says his agenda focuses on lowering costs for working families, including expanded childcare, more affordable healthcare and more housing supply.
Says he wants to expand coverage through the CT Option and lower prescription drug prices.
Signed Connecticut's Trust Act, described as reining in ICE activities, and criticized ICE arrests of parents in Danbury.
Says he would expand universal pre-K and affordable childcare, continue universal free school meals and increase state support for special education.
Says he aims for a 100% zero-carbon electricity grid by 2040 and net-zero emissions by 2050.
Says he supports protecting reproductive freedom and abortion access and has signed legislation doing so.

candidates.name: Ryan Fazio
candidates.bio: Ryan Fazio is a Republican state senator from Greenwich who first won his seat in a special election in August 2021 and represents Greenwich and New Canaan. Before running for office he worked as a commodities trader and then an investment adviser, and he has an economics degree from Northwestern University.

positions.summary: Says he would cut state income tax rates for about $2.5 billion in annual relief and put caps on property taxes.
Says the Trust Act undermines public safety and that a man who had served jail time should have been transferred to federal authorities for removal.
Favors school choice and charter schools.
Says he would cut electricity bills by 20% by ending hidden taxes, expanding reliable supply and removing mandates.
Says "I support keeping abortion legal," and says he voted against a bill protecting out-of-state patients because he thought it would compromise safety standards.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Summary note moved: vote shares were from a partial count (about 90%).
